title: Inconsistent Aggregation Readings
summary: Three aggregation links carry 110 Mbps. A failed link is forced to zero while the old differences remain, producing an impossible system until a backup is modelled.
concept: Forcing one variable to zero can contradict measurements that were perfectly consistent before the failure. The backup route must be written as a new variable, not silently ignored.

variables.meaning: Traffic on aggregation link C / restored backup (Mbps)

normal.label: Normal state
normal.description: All three links are healthy and carry 50, 35 and 25 Mbps.

failed.label: Link failed
failed.description: Link C reports zero while the logs still claim x₂ − x₃ = 10 and a 110 Mbps total. The three statements cannot hold together.

corrected.label: Corrected (simulated)
corrected.description: A backup path carries the 25 Mbps that link C can no longer carry. The two remaining links keep their original split.

teachingNotes: The failed stage is inconsistent because the old relationship x₂ − x₃ = 10 still expects traffic on a dead link.
The corrected model changes the equations to describe the backup path; it does not change the measured demand.
This recovery is a classroom simulation and does not repair physical hardware.
